## Overview

ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00781391) compared two once-daily [edoxaban](./edoxaban.md) regimens with [warfarin](./warfarin.md) in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation, with a median follow-up of 2.8 years. Each edoxaban regimen was tested for noninferiority to warfarin during the treatment period, with stroke or systemic embolism as the primary efficacy end point and major bleeding as the principal safety end point ([src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a.md)).

## Reported results

During treatment the primary end point occurred at 1.50% per year with warfarin (median time in the therapeutic range 68.4%), 1.18% with high-dose edoxaban and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban. Major bleeding occurred at 3.43% with warfarin, 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban ([src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a.md)).

The trial was funded by Daiichi Sankyo Pharma Development and is one of the four trials pooled in the meta-analysis of new oral anticoagulants ([src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a.md), [src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).
